This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.795/2009 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thrissur (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 11/05/2018.

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 22/12/2008 at about 02:00 p.m., while he was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-9/J-2151 ridden by the second respondent through Cheruthuruthy-Kulappully public road and when they reached near Chuduvalathur service station,
the motorcycle collided with another motorcycle bearing registration 2025:KER:50444 no.KL-9/P-6734, as a result of which both of them fell down and he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent-owner and the second respondent-rider remained ex-parte.

sentences.text: The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying the negligence on the part of the second respondent.
The amount of compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A10 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-rider of the offending motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,51,485/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with 2025:KER:50444 proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the notional income of the claim petitioner, a coolie aged 42 years, ought to have been fixed as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd, (2011)
13 SCC 236.

sentences.text:
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent-insurer that the income claimed was 6,000/-, which has been granted by the Tribunal and therefore it calls for no further enhancement by this Court.
2025:KER:50444 9.1.
It is true that the amount claimed in the petition is 6,000/- and the Tribunal has granted the amount also.

In the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), where the income of a coolie in the year 2008 was liable to be fixed at 6,500/-, I find that the notional income in this case can also be fixed at 6,500/-.
Percentage of disability 10.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that though Ext.A10 disability certificate dated 18/11/2016 was produced, the Tribunal did not consider the same or fix the disability accordingly.
Therefore he submits that on the basis of Ext.A10, the functional disability may be fixed as 38.17%.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent-insurer that Ext.A10 certificate issued by a single doctor could not have been relied on by the Tribunal and hence the reason why the same was not considered by the Tribunal.
He also points out that it was the burden of the claim petitioner to prove the disabilities caused as the result of the injuries sustained 2025:KER:50444 in the accident.

In this case, the claim petitioner has not entered the box or adduced any evidence to substantiate his claim that due to the injuries caused,
disabilities have been caused which affected his functioning or working as a coolie.
It is also pointed out that Ext.A4 discharge card shows that the wire was removed on 07/07/2009.

However, the Abdul Rahman vs Ayshabi on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10860765/
3 doctor in Ext.A10 has stated that the implant is in situ.

This itself would show that the doctor had not properly examined the claim petitioner or the records in the case before issuing the certificate,
goes the argument.
10.1. Ext.A10 dated 08/11/2016 is seen marked without any objection on behalf of the third respondent-insurer.
Ext.A10 reads thus - " Permanent disability certificate.

I Dr.T.G. Gopinathan, Consultant Orthopaedic surgeon have carefully examined Mr.
Abdul Rahman aged 47 years, S/o Saithali, Marath Prambu House, P.O. Keralassery,
Palakkad district, whose signature is given here and who is identified by photo in Electoral Card on 08/xi/16 for assessing his permanent disability sustained in an alleged RTA on 22/12/2008 and was initially treated Sevana Hospital,
2025:KER:50444 Pattambi and later at Government Medical College Hospital Thrissur.
His available hospital records WC copy, Discharge summary copies and X-ray show that (also discharge certificate for police cases) he sustained open reduction temporal lateral condylar fracture patella this was treated by ORIF.
Now the fracture has healed with implants in situ.

Present problem 1. Loss of ROM  knee- 70%
2. Wasting of  thigh muscles with loss of muscle power- grade III (Grade three only).
3. Loss of stability  lower limb - (cross legged sitting, squatting-standing on operated limb and climbing step difficult)
To sum up PD 1. Loss of ROM  knee- 70%.

21% 
2. Loss of muscle power  thigh - gr III -40% 12%
3. Loss of stability  lower limb - 40%.
12% His permanent disability is 38.17% to the part and 13.36% to whole body.
Certified that I have not treated this patient and I have a standing experience of more than 25 years in the field of Orthopaedics.

The central Government Ministry of Welfare and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is 2025:KER:50444 followed in calculating the percentage of Abdul Rahman vs Ayshabi on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10860765/

(Emphasis supplied) 10.2.

sentences.text: Here it would be apposite to refer Ext.A4 discharge cards.
The relevant portion of the discharge card dated 16/07/2009 reads thus- " CLINICAL DATA
Open knee injury earlier treated.
Admitted for, wire removal done on 07/07/2009.
SR done on 16/07/2009.
The relevant portion of the discharge card dated 09/02/2009 reads thus- " CLINICAL DATA
Referred from Sevana hospital with h/o alleged RTA, treated for intercondylar fracture (Rl) femur and open knee injury, by wound debridement repeated dressing and POP cast.
Later fitted with knee brace when wound was found to be clean..................."
10.3. The fact that the implant was removed on 07/07/2009 is evident from Ext.A4.
Therefore, the statement in Ext.A10 that the implant is still in place is apparently wrong.

This 2025:KER:50444 itself raises doubts as to whether the doctor who issued Ext.A10 had infact properly examined the claim petitioner or the medical records of the claim petitioner before issuing the certificate.
However, taking into account the injuries sustained, it appears that he has difficulty in sitting cross legged, squatting, standing on operated limb and difficulty in climbing steps.
The accident is not disputed.
Therefore, being a coolie, this would certainly have affected his functioning.
The Act being a beneficial legislation, the rejection of the certificate in toto may lead to injustice as the fact that accident took place and he sustained injuries are not disputed.

Hence, I find that the functional disability can be fixed as 13.36%.
